title: Bandwidth Control rules: terms, order and rank

prose.text: A rule ties bandwidth classes to enforcement terms. {{rule-terms}} The terms themselves, and how minimum and maximum behave, are in [[zia.bandwidth-control.allocation]].

prose.label: Does the rule apply to this traffic?
prose.text: {{criteria-expression}} {{criteria-expression-adding-page}} The two pages group Locations and Location Groups differently {{divergence:locations-location-groups-operator}}. {{non-matching-location-or-time-skips-rule}} Location scope is covered in [[zia.bandwidth-control.location-scope]].

prose.label: Writing a rule.
prose.text: {{scope-limits}} {{name-and-description-length}} The location limit differs between sources: [[zia.bandwidth-control.api-surface:locations-per-rule]].

prose.label: Order.
prose.text: {{ascending-order}} {{order-is-priority}} Whether the order matches the first-match-wins model of [[zia.url-filtering.rule-order]] is open {{gap:multi-rule-class}}. The default rule's fixed last position is in [[zia.bandwidth-control.default-rule]].

prose.label: Disabled rules and rank.
prose.text: {{disabled-holds-slot}} {{new-rule-disabled}} {{admin-rank}} {{admin-rank-range}} Provider reorder and rank behavior for bandwidth rules is in [[zia.terraform.rule-order.registry]].

checks.do: Whether the rule is enabled, since a disabled rule keeps its place in the order but is not enforced.
Whether the rule's location and time criteria match the traffic, stating that the pages differ on how Locations and Location Groups combine rather than choosing one.
Whether an earlier rule holds the same class, since bandwidth is allocated by rule order.
Whether the location enforces Bandwidth Control and has limits, since rules do not shape its traffic otherwise.

rule-terms.statement: Each rule defines a maximum and minimum bandwidth for the bandwidth classes in the rule, along with other parameters such as location and time of day.

quotes: Each rule defines a maximum and minimum bandwidth for the bandwidth classes in the rule along with other parameters, like location and time of day.

criteria-expression.statement: Rule conditions are grouped: Locations OR Location Groups, AND Time, AND (Bandwidth Classes AND Protocols). The relationship between the categories is AND.

quotes: The logical relationship between the categories is AND
Where [ Locations OR Location Groups ] AND
When: [ Time ] AND
What: [ Bandwidth Classes AND Protocols ]

ascending-order.statement: Bandwidth Control rules are evaluated in ascending numerical rule order, and the default rule is evaluated last.

quotes: Bandwidth Control rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order and the default rule is evaluated last.

expect.description: Rule order. Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on), and the Rule Order reflects this rule’s place in the order. You can change the value, but if you've enabled the Admin Rank, your assigned admin rank determines the Rule Order values you can select.

order-is-priority.statement: Bandwidth is allocated by rule order, so classes that need priority, such as business-critical applications, belong near the top of the rules.

quotes: Bandwidth is allocated based on the rule order.
Therefore, bandwidth classes such as business-critical applications, O365, etc. that require priority Bandwidth Control should be placed at the top of the rule sets.

disabled-holds-slot.statement: A disabled Bandwidth Control rule is not enforced but keeps its place in the rule order, and the service skips it and moves to the next rule.

expect.description: Indicates whether the rule is enabled or disabled. An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.

admin-rank.statement: With admin ranking enabled in Advanced Settings the rule list shows an Admin Rank column, and the admin rank limits the rule order values an administrator can select.

quotes: Admin Rank: The assigned admin rank for the rule. This is only visible if you have enabled admin ranking in the Advanced Settings.

expect.description: Rule order. Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on), and the Rule Order reflects this rule’s place in the order. You can change the value, but if you've enabled the Admin Rank, your assigned admin rank determines the Rule Order values you can select.

criteria-expression-adding-page.statement: The Adding Rules article joins the categories with AND and groups the conditions as Where: [Locations AND Location Groups], When: Time, and What: [Protocols AND Bandwidth Classes].

quotes: The logical relationship between the categories is AND, and the rule conditions within each category have their own set of logical operators applied, explained as follows:
- Where: [ Locations AND Location Groups ] AND
- When: Time AND
- What: [ Protocols AND Bandwidth Classes ] AND

scope-limits.statement: A rule takes Any or up to 32 locations, which must have Bandwidth Control enabled with download and upload limits; the article says to contact Zscaler Support to increase the default limit for Locations. Location Groups take Any or up to 32 and, if none is selected, the field is Any by default and the criterion is ignored during policy evaluation. Time takes up to two time intervals and is Always by default. Any number of bandwidth classes can be selected once URLs or cloud applications have been added to predefined or custom bandwidth classes.

quotes: Locations: Select Any to apply this rule to all locations, or select up to 32 locations.
You must enable Bandwidth Control for these locations and specify the download and upload bandwidth limits for each location.
Contact Zscaler Support to increase the default limit for Locations.
Location Groups: Select Any to apply the rule to all location groups, or select up to 32 location groups.
If you do not select specific location groups, the field is set to Any by default, and this criterion is ignored during policy evaluation.
Time: Select up to two time intervals during which the rule applies. By default, the field is set to Always.
You first must add URLs or cloud applications to predefined or custom bandwidth classes. Select any number of bandwidth classes.

name-and-description-length.statement: The rule name is system-generated and can be edited, and cannot exceed 63 characters. The description cannot exceed 10,240 characters. A rule label is optional.

quotes: Rule Name: A system-generated rule name is automatically populated, and the name can be edited. The name cannot exceed 63 characters.
The description cannot exceed 10,240 characters.
Rule Label: (Optional) Click Add Rule Label and select a label from the drop-down menu.

admin-rank-range.statement: Admin Rank is 0 to 7, with 0 the highest, and the option appears if Admin Ranking is enabled on the Advanced Settings page. An admin cannot select a rank higher than their own, and a rule with a higher admin rank always precedes a rule with a lower one.

quotes: Admin Rank: Click Edit and select an admin rank 0 to 7 (0 is the highest rank) from the drop-down menu. This option appears if you enable Admin Ranking on the Advanced Settings page.
Your assigned admin rank determines the values you can select (e.g., you cannot select a rank higher than your own).
The rule's admin rank determines the value you can select for rule order, so that a rule with a higher admin rank always precedes a rule with a lower admin rank.

new-rule-disabled.statement: A new rule's status is Disabled by default and the rule must be enabled to be enforced on traffic. Disabled rules can be assigned a rule order, and during evaluation the service skips them and moves to the successive ones.

quotes: Rule Status: By default, the status is Disabled. You need to enable the rule to activate and enforce it on your traffic.
Disabled rules can have a rule order assigned. During evaluation, the service skips the disabled rules and moves to the successive ones.

non-matching-location-or-time-skips-rule.statement: When a Bandwidth Control rule lists locations or a time window, it does not apply to traffic from another location or outside that window, however well the traffic's class and protocol match.
non-matching-location-or-time-skips-rule.conditions: Follows from the conditions being ANDed across Locations or Location Groups, Time, and Bandwidth Classes with Protocols.

locations-location-groups-operator.summary: How Locations and Location Groups combine in a Bandwidth Control rule: OR on the Configuring page, AND on the Adding Rules page.

quotes: Where [ Locations OR Location Groups ] AND

positions.says: Where [ Locations OR Location Groups ] AND.

quotes: - Where: [ Locations AND Location Groups ] AND

positions.says: Where: [ Locations AND Location Groups ] AND.

locations-location-groups-operator.impact: A rule that lists both Locations and Location Groups matches traffic from either under one reading and only traffic in both under the other; the pages do not say which governs.

multi-rule-class.title: A class referenced by more than one rule
multi-rule-class.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Rules are first-match-wins in ascending Rule Order. ... Same order-model as URL Filtering and Firewall.' The captured pages describe a top-to-bottom allocation in two passes, not a stop-at-first-match walk, and none states which rule's minimum and maximum apply when the same class appears in two rules.
multi-rule-class.blocks: deterministic answers about which rule shapes a class that two rules reference
